note.en: BJJ's americana is ude-garami with the hand pointing up towards the head.
BJJ's kimura, named for Masahiko Kimura, is the reverse form with the hand pointing down towards the hips.

about.en: The entangled armlock: uke's bent arm is wrapped in a figure-four of tori's arms and rotated against the shoulder and elbow. Applied with the hand up or down, which BJJ names as two techniques. Competition joint locks are restricted to the elbow and to senior age groups; learn and practise this only under instruction.

en: Figure-four grip: your hands lock through each other around their bent arm
Keep their elbow pinned; rotate the whole frame, do not push the wrist
Slow, small movements; the shoulder gives little warning
Your partner is on their back and you are at their right side, chest low over theirs.
Pin their left wrist to the mat with your left hand, their arm bent at a right angle, knuckles pointing up past their head.
Thread your right arm under their upper arm and grip your own left wrist: the figure-four that names the entanglement.
Keep their elbow and wrist both pinned, your chest heavy on theirs.

Apply by sliding their elbow down towards their body while your framed arms rotate the whole arm gently; the pressure turns the shoulder. Movements are small and slow, and everything releases the instant they tap.

receiving.en: Your bent arm is pinned and a second arm threads beneath it, locking into a frame; the rotation that follows loads your shoulder more than your elbow. Tap clearly at the first feeling of pressure; a shoulder can be injured before the pain becomes severe, and tolerates a late tap even less than an elbow. Never snatch out of a lock with a twist.

viNotes.en: A figure-four is easy to confirm without looking: your own wrist in your own hand. Pin their wrist to the mat first with the arm bent, then thread the other arm and clasp. The pressure turns the shoulder rather than straightening the elbow, so it arrives differently from a straight lock: small movements, chest heavy, everything released at the tap.

cue.en: The bent arm is wrapped in a figure-four of the attacker's arms and turned against shoulder and elbow.
